The Drowned Lighthouse

The beam still turns. Nobody has turned it on in eleven years.

Everything from here to the end of the page is raw HTML written by whoever shared this vault. None of it survives as markup. What survives is the prose around it, and — where the element’s own text was not itself the payload — that text.

A block-level raw HTML element takes its content with it, not just its tags. This is goldmark’s own rule — an HTML block is one unit, and without WithUnsafe() the whole unit is dropped — and it is worth stating plainly because it is the one case where a page loses an author’s words:

The same construct inline keeps its text, because an inline run is only the tags:

An inline element keeps this sentence in a paragraph.

A script block is the same rule and the most consequential instance:

As is a style block:

An inline script inside a generic container leaves its text behind, because there is nothing to execute once the tags are gone. The tags are the danger, and they are gone:

alert(2)

alert(3)

An iframe, an object, a form, a base element, and a comment — each dropped whole:

An author’s raw HTML is not filtered — it is not interpreted. goldmark never turns it into markup, so there is nothing for a sanitiser to remove and nothing for an author to smuggle. Both of these vanish whole, tags and text alike:

The markdown forms are how an author writes a picture or a link, and the policy is what bounds them rather than the author. Both of these survive:

An external link

And the second one carries no target, no rel, and no author-chosen class, because the policy allows none of the three.

The prose after all of that is intact, and so is the heading above it.
